stories.headline: Carney travels to China for APEC summit, floating Chinese auto investment amid US trade talks
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney is heading to China to meet with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen to deepen bilateral trade and economic ties. Ahead of the meeting, Carney indicated that Canada could look to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with the United States fail to preserve an integrated North American market, though he reaffirmed his preference for a continental approach. The diplomatic visit comes as Canadian exports to China have jumped nearly 40 per cent over the past year.

stories.headline: Canada and international allies urge Israel to permit critical winter aid into Gaza
stories.summary: Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, and Italy issued a joint diplomatic statement demanding that Israel grant immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access into Gaza. The coalition expressed urgent alarm that 150,000 emergency tents and other vital life-saving supplies remain blocked at border checkpoints ahead of winter. Calling the deepening humanitarian crisis entirely reversible, the four nations called for an end to border restrictions.

stories.headline: Mark Carney and Quebec Premier St-Pierre Plamondon hold first meeting at Francophonie summit
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney met with Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon for the first time during the Francophonie summit in Cambodia. Discussions centered on provincial outreach to the United States, bilateral trade, federal assistance for tackling homelessness, and an upcoming 2027 economic summit in Quebec. Both leaders described the meeting as constructive, agreeing to establish direct communication lines despite lingering jurisdictional tensions over foreign outreach.

stories.headline: Internal federal memo warns mounting freshwater shortages threaten Canada's long-term security
stories.summary: An internal federal government memo warns that growing pressures on Canada's freshwater supply pose a serious threat to the country's long-term security and economic prosperity. The document cites climate change, pollution, and rising demand as primary factors straining water resources across jurisdictions. Officials stress that failing to manage these escalating supply challenges leaves uncertainty over Canada's future water security.

stories.headline: Border agency demotes dozens of officers medically unable to carry sidearms
stories.summary: The Canada Border Services Agency has notified 63 frontline officers that they are being reassigned to lower-paying positions due to medical conditions preventing them from carrying duty firearms. The demotions follow an enforcement of mandatory sidearm requirements for armed border personnel, regardless of individual medical accommodations. The move has drawn scrutiny from affected staff and labour representatives over the agency's duty to accommodate injured or disabled workers.

stories.headline: Canada's largest federal public service union to hold nationwide strike votes
stories.summary: The Public Service Alliance of Canada, the federal government's largest public sector union, is launching information sessions and strike authorization votes that will run through January 22. While labour observers note an actual walkout is not guaranteed, the strike mandate votes significantly raise the likelihood of widespread disruption across federal departments. The escalating dispute centers on ongoing bargaining impasses over wages, workplace conditions, and return-to-office directives.

articles.title: Le plus gros syndicat de fonctionnaires fédéraux se prononcera sur un mandat de grève
articles.angle: Announces the scheduling of information meetings and strike mandate voting through late January

stories.headline: Federal Green Party elects former MP Mike Morrice as new leader
stories.summary: The Green Party of Canada has chosen former parliamentarian Mike Morrice as its new leader following an uncontested leadership race. Morrice declared that the party will concentrate on lowering the cost of living while confronting major oil and gas corporations. His election marks a rebuilding phase for the federal Greens as they attempt to regain parliamentary influence and voter traction.

stories.headline: Canada faces criticism at COP31 over fossil fuel transition and Alberta methane rules
stories.summary: Canada's environmental delegation at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey is facing intense pushback over its refusal to present a definitive roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. While federal officials sought to present the country as a global frontrunner in curbing methane emissions, policy experts argue that federal credibility is undercut by Alberta's lag in adopting equivalent provincial regulations. The divide highlights enduring intergovernmental friction over the speed of national decarbonization.

stories.headline: Meta pledges to defy federal orders if proposed lawful-access bill weakens encryption
stories.summary: Meta has announced it will reject any Canadian government directive that would compel the company to undermine encryption protocols on its platforms, as Parliament resumes debate on the Strong Borders Act. The federal government's proposed lawful-access legislation seeks powers to mandate electronic service providers modify systems to grant authorities access to digital communications. The clash underscores escalating tension between federal national security initiatives and major tech companies over privacy protections.

stories.headline: Ottawa plans up to 200,000 permanent residency spots for Hong Kong and Ukrainian nationals
stories.summary: A new federal immigration initiative aims to fast-track permanent residency approvals for up to 200,000 Hong Kong and Ukrainian nationals currently living in Canada. The program offers long-awaited clarity to thousands of temporary residents who have faced lengthy processing backlogs after fleeing conflict and political instability. The measure represents a targeted adjustment to federal immigration targets to transition established temporary residents into permanent status.

articles.author: Kamil Karamali
articles.title: Canada plans up to 200,000 extra permanent residence spaces. Here’s who could benefit

stories.headline: Ontario legislation proposes expanding garbage incineration for energy amid landfill capacity crunch
stories.summary: The Ford government has introduced sweeping legislation that could facilitate burning more waste across Ontario to generate electricity and alleviate shrinking landfill space. Proponents argue incineration addresses an imminent disposal crisis, but environmental critics warn the policy will degrade air quality and undercut waste diversion initiatives. The bill sets up an impending debate at Queen's Park over provincial waste management and emission targets.

articles.author: Shawn Jeffords
articles.title: Provincial bill could pave the way for more trash incineration to make energy

stories.headline: Pfizer withdraws hormone therapy drug from Canada, raising coverage concerns in Ontario
stories.summary: Pfizer has removed its hormone replacement therapy Premarin from the Canadian market, eliminating the primary government-funded treatment for certain menopause symptoms. Medical professionals warn that the remaining alternative cream is not currently covered under Ontario's public drug program, creating significant out-of-pocket costs for patients. Advocates are calling on provincial health authorities to urgently update the provincial formulary to ensure accessible care.

articles.author: Alex Arsenych
articles.title: Pfizer pulls hormone therapy drug from Canada, leaving only one option that’s not covered in Ontario

stories.headline: Government insiders question Premier Ford's push to overhaul Niagara Falls casinos
stories.summary: Internal pushback has emerged around Premier Doug Ford's plan to overhaul casino operations in Niagara Falls, with sources close to the premier expressing deep skepticism over the project. While Ford maintains that existing revenue and operational models are unacceptable, insiders have privately criticized his continued focus on the gaming file. The disagreement exposes rare friction over provincial commercial and gaming priorities.

articles.author: Moira Welsh
articles.title: Insiders on Doug Ford's Niagara Falls casino dream: 'Everyone knows it's a dumb idea'

stories.headline: Appeal by former top RCMP official Cameron Ortis asserts secrecy hindered defence
stories.summary: Former senior RCMP intelligence official Cameron Ortis is appealing his conviction at the Ontario Court of Appeal, arguing that stringent state secrecy laws severely restricted his legal defence. Ortis's counsel claims that strict limitations on disclosing sensitive intelligence material impaired his constitutional right to make full answer and defence during trial. The appeal hearing, scheduled for February, will test the balance between national security confidentiality and fair trial rights in Canadian courts.

articles.author: David Ebner
articles.title: Secrecy in case of former top RCMP official curtailed defence, appeal asserts

stories.headline: Ontario's appointment of regional 'strong chairs' triggers backlash from GTA mayors
stories.summary: Tensions are mounting between local municipal leaders and Queen's Park following the Ontario government's appointment of eight regional chairs vested with powers to override municipal councils. Several mayors across the Greater Toronto Area are pushing back, arguing the centralized authority undermines local democratic governance and municipal autonomy. The dispute threatens to strain regional cooperation over housing, transit, and infrastructure planning.

articles.author: Alyshah Hasham
articles.title: Why Doug Ford’s ‘strong chairs’ have some Toronto-area mayors spoiling for a fight

stories.headline: Canadian travellers launch legal action after falling victim to Pearson airport luggage tag switching
stories.summary: More than two dozen Canadian travellers falsely accused of international drug smuggling are taking legal action, alleging corrupt airport workers switched their checked luggage tags onto bags filled with narcotics. Victims say their complaints were dismissed by authorities after illicit shipments were routed under their names at Toronto Pearson International Airport. A proposed fix has emerged as plaintiffs seek accountability from airport operators and security agencies.

stories.headline: Toronto Police investigate alleged assault of Falun Gong protesters outside Chinese consulate
stories.summary: Toronto Police have launched an investigation into a video showing an alleged assault against two Falun Gong demonstrators outside the Chinese consulate in Toronto. The incident, where an assailant allegedly claimed the site was Chinese territory, has triggered renewed demands from advocacy groups for the federal government to confront Beijing. Community leaders are urging Prime Minister Mark Carney to raise the issue of transnational repression during his diplomatic engagements in China.

articles.author: Judy Trinh
articles.title: ‘This is Chinese territory’: Toronto Police investigate alleged assault outside Chinese Consulate

stories.headline: TTC implements winter ban on e-bikes and e-scooters to prevent battery fires
stories.summary: The Toronto Transit Commission has enacted its seasonal ban prohibiting e-bikes and e-scooters from all transit vehicles and properties until April 15. The annual policy is designed to reduce the risk of transit fires stemming from volatile lithium-ion batteries during cold weather conditions. Transit authorities are advising commuters who rely on micromobility devices to plan alternative travel arrangements throughout the winter season.

stories.headline: Defence contractor Roshel acquires idle Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton
stories.summary: Canadian defence manufacturer Roshel has purchased an idle automotive assembly plant in Brampton, Ontario, from Stellantis to expand its military vehicle manufacturing capacity. The facility, which has sat unused for several years, will be repurposed to help Roshel meet surging domestic and international defence procurement orders. The acquisition provides a significant economic boost to Peel Region's industrial manufacturing sector.

articles.author: The Canadian Press
articles.title: Defence contractor Roshel looking to build capacity, meet demand with plant purchase

stories.headline: Two construction workers killed after being struck by out-of-control vehicle in Pickering
stories.summary: Durham Regional Police report that two construction workers were killed when an out-of-control Tesla struck them at a work site in Pickering, east of Toronto. Emergency crews responded to the scene, but both victims succumbed to their injuries. Investigators are probing the cause of the collision, including vehicle mechanics and driver actions, while provincial workplace safety authorities review construction site safety protocols.

articles.author: The Canadian Press
articles.title: Two people dead after crash involving out-of-control Tesla: Durham police
